answer: Each identity stewards one bridge span, locking a 70-credit bond. A quartz gauge records deflection; a velvet strip under the joint is replaced under a fresh serial. The steward files these each epoch. An auditor recomputes deflection from traffic count and span-load table; a reading off by over 2 percent or a reused serial burns the bond. First filing 36, kth fake 36+7(k-1), 1000th 7029; 1000 fakes cost 3,532,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented gauge fails: it is bound to its span, and the strip serial is consumed. An honest steward pays 36 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
